lead_headline: Arvada Renews 10-Year Comcast Franchise, Upgrades PEG Fees and Insurance Terms

type_specific.meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council met on July 21, 2026, beginning with a meeting of the Arvada Housing Authority, which approved its annual report, 2027 PHA plan, and Housing Choice Voucher Program administrative plan updates. The council then addressed a range of business items including an unscheduled external audit presentation, multiple public hearings on topics spanning a Comcast franchise renewal to a gravel driveway variance and an industrial annexation, and approved an intergovernmental agreement establishing the Clear Creek Trail Collaborative. Multiple public commenters spoke in support of Frontline Farming, an urban farm operating at Majestic View Park whose lease status appears to be under dispute.

tonight_at_a_glance.synopsis: Council approved a renewed 10-year Comcast cable franchise with improved financial terms, joined the Clear Creek Trail Collaborative, approved a gravel driveway variance for a historic property, and annexed and rezoned a 5.4-acre industrial parcel. The city's external auditors reported a clean opinion with one material weakness at the urban renewal authority.
highlights: Renewed 10-year Comcast cable franchise with higher insurance minimums and a revenue-based PEG fee model
Approved IGA joining the 15-agency Clear Creek Trail Collaborative for the 65-mile regional trail
Granted major modification allowing a recycled gravel driveway at a historic 1890s property with a new ADU
Annexed, rezoned, and approved conditional use for a 5.4-acre Revival Industrial parcel near Highway 72
External auditors from Plante Moran delivered a clean (unmodified) audit opinion; one material weakness noted at the urban renewal authority has been corrected

presentations.presenter_role: Housing Authority Staff, City of Arvada
prose_paragraphs: Espinosa reported that the Housing Authority served an average of 522 households over the past 12 months (down from 535 the prior year due to HUD budget constraints), spent $9.1 million in rental assistance, and has approximately 3,950 families on the wait list. Notable milestones include the opening of Marshall Street Landing (85 units of permanent supportive housing), the lease-up of Legacy Senior Residences (72 senior units), and two projects under construction: Marshall Point Apartments (72 units, projected October 2027 opening) and Griffith Station Town Homes (20 affordable homeownership units via Habitat for Humanity). The authority also added a housing case manager funded by DOLA dollars and received word from HUD that new vouchers will soon be available, reversing last year's projected shortfall.

presentations.topic: External Audit Results — City of Arvada FY 2025
prose_paragraphs: Plante Moran auditors presented findings from the city's FY 2025 financial audit to the full council following an earlier presentation to the audit committee. The city received an unmodified (clean) opinion on its nearly 200-page financial statements, the highest level of assurance available. The single audit of $11.4 million in federal expenditures — including $9.9 million in housing voucher cluster spending — also received a clean opinion with no findings. One material weakness was identified related to a segregation of duties in cash disbursements at the Arvada Urban Renewal Authority; management represented the issue has already been corrected.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-051 A resolution authorizing a communication site lease amendment by and between the city of Arvada and T-Mobile West LLC, formerly Clear Wire LLC 7710 Reno Drive.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Approves an amendment to a lease agreement allowing T-Mobile (formerly ClearWire) to continue using a city-owned communications site at 7710 Reno Drive.

consent_agenda.official_title: R26-052 A resolution authorizing an Adams County open space grant agreement regarding the Tennyson complete and connected corridor.
consent_agenda.plain_english_summary: Authorizes rescinding and reissuing a modified Adams County Open Space grant for the Tennyson corridor, reflecting a reduction of approximately $625,000 after Adams County reclaimed certain project elements it took back in 2022. This formalizes an arrangement already approved by the council in March 2026.

resolutions.official_title: R26-053 A resolution authorizing approval of an intergovernmental agreement establishing the Clear Creek Trail Collaborative.
resolutions.plain_english_summary: Arvada joins a voluntary 15-agency collaborative managing the 65-mile Clear Creek Trail from the South Platte River to Loveland Pass. Arvada participates as an advisory (non-voting) member with no financial obligations under this agreement.

ordinances.official_title: CB26-021 An ordinance approving the renewal of a non-exclusive franchise agreement for the use of city rights of way with Comcast of California, Colorado, Florida, Oregon, Inc., ordinance number 4937.
ordinances.plain_english_summary: Renews Comcast's cable franchise for 10 years, raising the commercial general liability insurance minimum from $1 million to $5 million, switching PEG fee collection to 0.33% of monthly gross revenue (up from $0.50/subscriber), and clarifying that the franchise is subject to the city's police powers rather than the reverse.

ordinances.official_title: CB26-022 An ordinance annexing certain land into the city of Arvada, Revival Industrial, a 5.3980 acre parcel of land approximately located south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72 in the city of Arvada, County of Jefferson, State of Colorado, ordinance number 4938.
ordinances.plain_english_summary: Annexes a 5.4-acre parcel near Highway 72 and Indiana Street from Jefferson County into Arvada, enabling development under city standards.

ordinances.official_title: CB26-023 An ordinance rezoning certain land within the city of Arvada Revival Industrial from Jefferson County SR-2 to City of Arvada MX-S mixed-use suburban and amending the official zoning maps of the city of Arvada, Colorado, a 5.3980 acre parcel of land approximately located south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72, ordinance number 4939.
ordinances.plain_english_summary: Rezones the newly annexed Revival Industrial parcel from Jefferson County SR-2 to Arvada's MX-S mixed-use suburban district, consistent with the city's comprehensive plan designation for this area.

ordinances.official_title: CB26-024 An ordinance approving a conditional use permit for Revival Industrial a 5.3980 acre parcel of land located approximately south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72 ordinance number 4940.
ordinances.plain_english_summary: Grants a conditional use permit allowing light industrial uses within the MX-S zoning district for the Revival Industrial site, enabling development of an approximately 56,000-square-foot commercial building serving manufacturers, distributors, and similar tenants.

This is a yearly report required by HUD summarizing the city's accomplishments from June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026 related to affordable housing and community development goals funded by the Community Development Block Grant. The city must submit the report to HUD by August 31, 2026. No council vote was required.

meeting_summary: The Arvada City Council met on July 21, 2026, beginning with a meeting of the Arvada Housing Authority, which approved its annual report, 2027 PHA plan, and Housing Choice Voucher Program administrative plan updates. The council then addressed a range of business items including an unscheduled external audit presentation, multiple public hearings on topics spanning a Comcast franchise renewal to a gravel driveway variance and an industrial annexation, and approved an intergovernmental agreement establishing the Clear Creek Trail Collaborative. Multiple public commenters spoke in support of Frontline Farming, an urban farm operating at Majestic View Park whose lease status appears to be under dispute.

key_decisions.significance: Staff to submit the CAPER report to HUD by August 31, 2026.

Staff acknowledged it is something they can look at.

R26-051 A resolution authorizing a communication site lease amendment by and between the city of Arvada and T-Mobile West LLC, formerly Clear Wire LLC 7710 Reno Drive.
key_decisions.significance: Approves an amendment to a lease agreement allowing T-Mobile (formerly ClearWire) to continue using a city-owned communications site at 7710 Reno Drive.

key_decisions.motion: R26-052 A resolution authorizing an Adams County open space grant agreement regarding the Tennyson complete and connected corridor.
key_decisions.significance: Authorizes rescinding and reissuing a modified Adams County Open Space grant for the Tennyson corridor, reflecting a reduction of approximately $625,000 after Adams County reclaimed certain project elements it took back in 2022. This formalizes an arrangement already approved by the council in March 2026.

key_decisions.motion: R26-053 A resolution authorizing approval of an intergovernmental agreement establishing the Clear Creek Trail Collaborative.
key_decisions.significance: Arvada joins a voluntary 15-agency collaborative managing the 65-mile Clear Creek Trail from the South Platte River to Loveland Pass. Arvada participates as an advisory (non-voting) member with no financial obligations under this agreement.

key_decisions.motion: CB26-021 An ordinance approving the renewal of a non-exclusive franchise agreement for the use of city rights of way with Comcast of California, Colorado, Florida, Oregon, Inc., ordinance number 4937.
key_decisions.significance: Renews Comcast's cable franchise for 10 years, raising the commercial general liability insurance minimum from $1 million to $5 million, switching PEG fee collection to 0.33% of monthly gross revenue (up from $0.50/subscriber), and clarifying that the franchise is subject to the city's police powers rather than the reverse.

key_decisions.motion: CB26-022 An ordinance annexing certain land into the city of Arvada, Revival Industrial, a 5.3980 acre parcel of land approximately located south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72 in the city of Arvada, County of Jefferson, State of Colorado, ordinance number 4938.
key_decisions.significance: Annexes a 5.4-acre parcel near Highway 72 and Indiana Street from Jefferson County into Arvada, enabling development under city standards.

key_decisions.motion: CB26-023 An ordinance rezoning certain land within the city of Arvada Revival Industrial from Jefferson County SR-2 to City of Arvada MX-S mixed-use suburban and amending the official zoning maps of the city of Arvada, Colorado, a 5.3980 acre parcel of land approximately located south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72, ordinance number 4939.
key_decisions.significance: Rezones the newly annexed Revival Industrial parcel from Jefferson County SR-2 to Arvada's MX-S mixed-use suburban district, consistent with the city's comprehensive plan designation for this area.

key_decisions.motion: CB26-024 An ordinance approving a conditional use permit for Revival Industrial a 5.3980 acre parcel of land located approximately south of State Highway 72 east of 15350 State Highway 72 ordinance number 4940.
key_decisions.significance: Grants a conditional use permit allowing light industrial uses within the MX-S zoning district for the Revival Industrial site, enabling development of an approximately 56,000-square-foot commercial building serving manufacturers, distributors, and similar tenants.
